title: Financial Media, Price Discovery, and Merger Arbitrage

rival_explanations: returns reflect efficient-market compensation for risk under a misspecified asset pricing model, not underreaction
the predictable returns are compensation for systematic risk
the arbitrage alpha reflects known merger-arbitrage risk premia / limits to arbitrage rather than media information
the predictive words are spurious artifacts of data dredging rather than economically meaningful content

context.country_region: United States (non-US companies removed to avoid cross-border mergers)
context.time_period: 1999-2009 (main sample; extended-sample robustness check runs through the beginning of 2016)
context.sample_description: Merger deals from Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum (disclosed value M&A, tender offers, exchange offers), with both target and acquirer being US public companies; challenged deals, self-tenders/recapitalizations, and strongly regulated industries excluded; keep deals completed or withdrawn where acquirer owns >50% after and purchases >=20% of shares; keep the largest 1,200 deals by deal value; matched to press articles from Dow Jones Factiva, stock data from CRSP, and accounting data from Compustat
context.sample_size: 1,107 mergers (after merging all databases; 130,589 press articles from Factiva)
